text:
The population ratio of two atomic levels in LTE follows the Boltzmann law  

\[
\frac{n_2}{n_1}= \frac{g_2}{g_1}\exp\!\left[-\frac{E_{21}}{kT}\right].
\]

The statistical‑weight factor \((g_2/g_1)\) is the same for both temperatures, so the change in the ratio depends only on the exponential term.

---

### 1. Energy difference of the Ti transition  

\[
\lambda = 1448\ \text{Å}=1.448\times10^{-7}\ \text{m}
\]

\[
E_{21}= \frac{hc}{\lambda}= \frac{6.626\times10^{-34}\,\text{J·s}\; \times 3.00\times10^{8}\,\text{m s}^{-1}}{1.448\times10^{-7}\,\text{m}}
          \approx 1.37\times10^{-18}\ \text{J}.
\]

\[
\frac{E_{21}}{k}= \frac{1.37\times10^{-18}}{1.381\times10^{-23}}\ \text{K}
                \approx 9.9\times10^{4}\ \text{K}.
\]

---

### 2. Spot and quiet‑region temperatures  

The star’s effective temperature with 40 % spot coverage is  

\[
T_{\rm eff}^{4}=f\,T_{\rm spot}^{4}+(1-f)T_{\rm quiet}^{4},
\qquad f=0.40,
\]

with \(T_{\rm eff}=5500\) K and \(T_{\rm quiet}=6000\) K.

Solving for \(T_{\rm spot}\):

\[
T_{\rm spot}^{4}= \frac{T_{\rm eff}^{4}-(1-f)T_{\rm quiet}^{4}}{f}
                \approx 3.44\times10^{14}\ \text{K}^{4},
\]
\[
T_{\rm spot}\approx 4.3\times10^{3}\ \text{K}.
\]

---

### 3. Level‑population ratios  

\[
R_{\rm quiet}= \exp\!\left(-\frac{9.9\times10^{4}}{6000}\right)=e^{-16.5}\approx 6.6\times10^{-8},
\]
\[
R_{\rm spot}= \exp\!\left(-\frac{9.9\times10^{4}}{4300}\right)=e^{-23.1}\approx 9.7\times10^{-11}.
\]

---

### 4. Observed (disk‑integrated) ratio  

The observed line strength is proportional to the continuum flux from each surface element (\(\propto T^{4}\)).  
Hence the flux‑weighted average ratio is  

\[
R_{\rm obs}= \frac{f\,T_{\rm spot}^{4}R_{\rm spot}+(1-f)\,T_{\rm quiet}^{4}R_{\rm quiet}}
                  {f\,T_{\rm spot}^{4}+(1-f)\,T_{\rm quiet}^{4}}.
\]

Using the numbers above:

\[
R_{\rm obs}\approx
\frac{0.4(3.44\times10^{14})(9.7\times10^{-11})+
      0.6(1.30\times10^{15})(6.6\times10^{-8})}
     {0.4(3.44\times10^{14})+0.6(1.30\times10^{15})}
\approx 5.6\times10^{-8}.
\]

---

### 5. Change factor  

\[
\frac{R_{\rm quiet}}{R_{\rm obs}} \approx
\frac{6.6\times10^{-8}}{5.6\times10^{-8}} \simeq 1.2.
\]

Thus the neutral‑Ti level‑population ratio is about **1.1–1.2 times larger** when the star has no spots compared with the spotted case.

The answer closest to this value is:

**(A) ~1.1**.  

Answer: A
